The evidence explicitly states that for binocular input, a stereo depth estimation model [11] is used to predict metric depth maps, and for monocular input, a monocular depth estimation model [25] is used to predict relative depth maps. The claim accurately reflects these facts.

It works for both binocular and monocular input sequences by leveraging depth estimation models to back-project pixels into world coordinates, creating a dense point cloud that serves as the initial state for Gaussian optimization [S1, unofficial].

The claim is fully supported by the evidence. The evidence states that the strategy works for both binocular and monocular inputs. For binocular input, it uses a stereo depth estimation model to predict metric depth maps and re-projects pixels into world coordinates to obtain a partial point cloud. For monocular input, it uses a monocular depth estimation model to predict relative depth maps and applies the same re-projection. The resulting points serve as the initialized state for Gaussian optimization, which is described as generating 'dense and accurate initialized points' (dense point cloud) within seconds.
